text.p: European Union Farm Commissioner Franz Fischler advocated the release of EU funds for flood-hit farmers in the eastern German state of Brandenburg, in an interview with German radio on Thursday.

Fischler said he was looking favourably at requests to reschedule autumn farm support payments for immediate pay-out. There was also discussion at EU Commission level whether structural aid totalling 44 million Ecus may be freed.
Farms that ran out of feed should be allowed to use set-aside land for grazing, he said.
Fischler also said Poland and the Czech republic would be able to draw on EU emergency aid programmes totalling up to 1.36 million Ecus.
Farm minister Jochen Borchert said on Monday he had requested aid for farmers from the EU Commission.
The EU on Wednesday proposed to provide 1.5 million Ecus in relief aid, mostly earmarked for repair of sewage and waste disposal systems and to ensure safe drinking water supply.

Flooded farming areas on Tuesday totalled 7,500 hectares and the damage bill to farmers was put at 50 million marks initially but new leaks in dikes in the so-called Oderbruch area overnight are threatening more homes and crops. --Hamburg newsroom, +49-40-41903275
